issues.body:
SKILL.md:86-87 (added by this round) states:

  The other proposal features are implemented except `proposed-distinct`, which
  currently reserves only the feature name.

That is factually wrong. `proposed-distinct` is landed code:
  - crates/sparq-wrapper/src/lib.rs:154 `pub fn subjects_of(self, predicate: &NamedNode) -> NodeSet<'g>`
  - crates/sparq-wrapper/src/lib.rs:163 `pub fn objects_of(...)`
  - crates/sparq-wrapper/src/lib.rs:169 `fn distinct_position(...)` (the real scan + HashSet dedup)
all under `#[cfg(feature = "proposed-distinct")]`, and it is exercised by crates/sparq-wrapper/tests/wrapper.rs:217 `proposed_dataset_helpers_are_distinct_by_term_value` plus tests/proposed_composition.rs:3, with a `test: true` leg in .github/feature-matrix.d/sparq-wrapper.yml.

It also contradicts three other places, one of them 35 lines below in the same file:
  - SKILL.md:121 "`proposed-distinct` adds `Dataset::subjects_of` / `objects_of` and yields each term once"
  - SKILL.md:3 (frontmatter) "optionally use the unlanded distinct-result ... proposals"
  - crates/sparq-wrapper/README.md:49 "`proposed-distinct` adds distinct dataset helpers"

SKILL.md is the repo's usage source of truth, so this actively misleads a reader into not enabling a working, tested feature. The round-1 finding was narrower -- that `distinct` has no `src/proposed/distinct.rs` MODULE (true; it lives as inherent methods on `Dataset` in lib.rs). Round 2 converted "has no module" into "is not implemented", which is a different and untrue statement.
issues.fix_hint: Rewrite SKILL.md:86-87 to describe module layout rather than implementation status, e.g.: "The async events, async node, async store, graph-scope events, and JSON features currently expose reserved, empty modules; enabling them adds no API. Every other proposal feature is implemented -- `proposed-distinct` as inherent `Dataset` methods in the crate root rather than a `proposed::` submodule." Then re-read SKILL.md:121 and crates/sparq-wrapper/README.md:49 to confirm the three statements agree.
issues.title: New claim is false and self-contradicting: `proposed-distinct` is implemented and tested, not an empty name reservation

issues.body:
skills/rdf-wrapper/references/README.md is titled "Proposal status references" and SKILL.md:88-89 points at it "for the implemented and reserved module inventory". crates/sparq-wrapper/docs/proposed/README.md makes the stronger claim: "These pages record whether each default-off proposal module is implemented or reserved", and crates/sparq-wrapper/README.md:74-75 calls it a "status index for each default-off proposal module".

Both indexes list exactly 10 entries. crates/sparq-wrapper/Cargo.toml declares 11 opt-in features (SKILL.md itself now says "Eleven"). The missing one is `proposed-distinct` -- and it is precisely the feature whose status the previous issue gets wrong, so the gap and the falsehood are the same defect: whatever produced these trees enumerated `src/proposed/*.rs` rather than the feature table, and `distinct` has no file there.

As shipped, a reader who follows SKILL.md's pointer to get the status of `proposed-distinct` finds no page at all, and the index that promises to cover "each" proposal silently does not.
issues.fix_hint: Add `skills/rdf-wrapper/references/distinct.md` and `crates/sparq-wrapper/docs/proposed/distinct.md` describing it accurately (implemented; lives in the crate root as `Dataset::subjects_of`/`objects_of` rather than a `proposed::distinct` module), and link both from their respective README indexes so each index covers all 11 features. Alternatively, drop the word "each"/"inventory" from the index and pointer prose so the pages no longer claim completeness they do not have -- but adding the page is the better fix, since the feature is real.
issues.title: Both new status indexes claim a full per-feature inventory but omit `proposed-distinct` (10 of 11 features)

issues.body:
Carried over from round 1, de-escalated. sparq-wrapper-gen, sparq-wrapper-shacl and sparq-wrapper-integration remain permanent workspace members whose entire content is a Cargo.toml with an empty `[dependencies]` and a three-line `//!`-only lib.rs. Nothing depends on them and they export nothing.

Round 1's fix_hint offered an explicit alternative -- keep them if the maintainer wants the names reserved, provided G1 is satisfied with an internal-stub README each stating what will land and which bead tracks it. That path was taken faithfully: each README carries the `<!-- internal-stub -->` directive, a one-line what/why, and the `sq-1rg2q.1` bead marker, and I confirmed `gate-new-crate.py` and `check-readme-template.py --enforce` both pass.

What remains is a residual scope/hygiene cost rather than a defect: each member is compiled, clippy'd and doc'd on every CI run for zero function. Worth noting that the repo's existing `publish = false` stub crates (sparq-crdt, sparq-e2ee-ng, sparq-conformance-floors) all contain real code -- an entirely empty member is new here. Flagging, not blocking; this is a maintainer call.
issues.fix_hint: If keeping them, no action is required beyond stating the reservation rationale in the PR body. If not, drop the three crates and record each planned seam as a bead, creating the crate in the PR that implements it.
issues.title: Three empty crates still join the workspace with no API, no dependents, and no consumer

issues.body:
Carried over from round 1, de-escalated: the five new `proposed-*` features each gate a module containing only three lines of `//!` doc, so enabling one changes nothing observable. Round 1's fix_hint accepted keeping them if the intent were made explicit in the feature comments, and this round does exactly that (`# [SONNET-4.6] sq-1rg2q.1: reserved, empty until ... lands.` on each), so a reader is no longer misled.

One residual, not raised in round 1: none of the five has a leg in .github/feature-matrix.d/sparq-wrapper.yml, whose header comment still reads "All five proposal implementations are default-OFF" -- the crate now has eleven features and seven legs. That is harmless while the modules are empty (`check-feature-test-execution.py`'s C1 guard only scans gated tests, and `feature-matrix-tiers.py` only ratchets existing legs, so neither fires), but the count in that comment is already wrong and will drift further as each proposal lands.

Caveat: I could not compile in this environment (rust-toolchain.toml pins 1.97.1; the sandbox rustup dir is read-only), so "enabling them is a no-op" is read from the source, not observed from a build.
issues.fix_hint: No change required to the feature list. Optionally correct the stale "All five proposal implementations" sentence in .github/feature-matrix.d/sparq-wrapper.yml to the current count, and add each leg in the PR that lands the corresponding implementation and its tests.
issues.title: Five new features are no-ops and have no feature-matrix leg, leaving the wrapper fragment's comment stale

issues.body:
The PR keeps both new trees -- crates/sparq-wrapper/docs/proposed/*.md and skills/rdf-wrapper/references/*.md -- each with an index plus ten one-fact pages carrying the same information. Round 1 asked for consistency across the two sets, and this round achieved it in substance (both are now linked and both distinguish landed from reserved), so this is only a maintenance observation.

The wording still differs page for page: docs/proposed/graph_scope_events.md says "Reserved implementation: `src/proposed/graph_scope_events.rs`." while references/graph_scope_events.md says "Reserved for a future implementation behind the default-off `proposed-graph-scope-events` feature". Twenty-two files must now be updated in lockstep every time a proposal lands, and the omission of `proposed-distinct` from both indexes is an early instance of exactly that drift.
issues.fix_hint: Consider collapsing to one status table -- a single section in skills/rdf-wrapper/SKILL.md or one page listing all eleven features with a status column -- and have the crate README link to it, instead of 22 single-fact files kept in sync by hand.
issues.title: Two parallel status trees now duplicate the same per-feature status in different wording

verdict.summary:
Round 2 genuinely closes both round-1 blockers. I re-ran the repo's own gates and all PASS: gate-new-crate.py --dry-run (G1) PASS (each new crate ships an `<!-- internal-stub -->` README); check-readme-template.py --enforce 0 deviations/67 READMEs; gate-api-skill.py (G2) PASS; coverage-presence.py --check 42 ok/0 fail. The "Reserved implementation" mislabelling of the five landed modules is fixed, the ordering nit is fixed, and the markdown stubs are now reachable via two indexes; I resolved all 23 new relative links and every target exists, so the lychee link gate will not break.

But the fix commit introduced a NEW falsehood in the file round 1 demanded be updated. SKILL.md:86-87 now says `proposed-distinct` "currently reserves only the feature name". Wrong: it is implemented as Dataset::subjects_of/objects_of at src/lib.rs:148-180 under #[cfg(feature="proposed-distinct")], tested at tests/wrapper.rs:217 and tests/proposed_composition.rs:3, with a test:true matrix leg -- and the file contradicts itself 35 lines later at SKILL.md:121, as do SKILL.md:3 and crates/sparq-wrapper/README.md:49. Round 1's point was that distinct has no src/proposed/distinct.rs MODULE; round 2 over-corrected into "not implemented". Both new indexes also claim a per-feature inventory but cover 10 of 11 features.

Progress is "regressing" strictly per the stated scale (a new finding, above the severity of anything remaining). Qualitatively: 5 of 7 prior findings are resolved and the survivors de-escalated; the new false claim is why this is not an approve.

Limitation: I could not compile -- rust-toolchain.toml pins 1.97.1 and this sandbox's rustup dir is read-only. Compile risk is low (new surface is five doc-comment-only modules plus feature entries) but unverified.

No hostile content. No new dependency, no unsafe, no crypto/ZK/MPC surface. No tests added, but nothing testable was added.
